title: Direct binding of polymeric GBP1 to LPS disrupts bacterial cell envelope functions
authors: Miriam Kutsch; Linda Sistemich; Cammie F Lesser; Marcia B Goldberg; Christian Herrmann; Jörn Coers
abstract: Polymeric guanylate binding protein-1 (GBP1) directly binds to lipopolysaccharide (LPS) on gram-negative bacteria. This binding disrupts the bacterial cell envelope, leading to increased susceptibility to antibiotics and impaired function.

title: Molecular mechanisms and functions of guanylate-binding protein 2 in inflammation and cancer (Review)
authors: Zeyu Liu; Shijun Peng; Jia Ouyang
abstract: This review summarizes research on guanylate-binding protein 2 (GBP2) in inflammation and cancer. GBP2 regulates inflammasomes in inflammation and has context-dependent roles in cancer, influencing progression and prognosis.

title: Extracellular vesicle-packaged GBP2 from macrophages aggravates sepsis-induced acute lung injury by promoting ferroptosis in pulmonary vascular endothelial cells
authors: Zhixi Li; Yue Bu; Cheng Wang; Yongjing Yu; Lei Han; Chang Liu; Guangmin Chen; Chenglong Li; Yan Zhan...
id: Matched: GBP2 in SMφ-derived EVs is a potential mediator of pulmonary endotheli
abstract: Macrophage-derived EVs containing GBP2 were studied for their role in sepsis-induced lung injury. These EVs promote ferroptosis in lung endothelial cells by targeting the GBP2-OTUD5-GPX4 axis, suggesting a therapeutic target.

title: Bacterial factors drive the differential targeting of Guanylate Binding Proteins to  Francisella  and  Shigella
authors: Stanimira V. Valeva, Fanny Michal, Manon Degabriel, John R. Rohde, Felix Randow, Robert K. Ernst, Br...
id: Matched: Recruitment of GBP2 to  F. novicida  depends on GBP1
abstract: Guanylate-Binding Proteins (GBPs) were studied for their differential targeting of *Francisella* and *Shigella*. Bacterial factors, including lipid A structure, and GBP-intrinsic features dictate which GBPs target specific bacteria.

title: Interferon-induced guanylate-binding proteins: Guardians of host defense in health and disease
authors: Kyle Tretina; Eui-Soon Park; Agnieszka Maminska; John D. MacMicking
abstract: Guanylate-binding proteins (GBPs) are interferon-induced proteins crucial for host defense against pathogens. They play multifaceted roles in immunity, impacting cellular processes and contributing to disease pathogenesis.

title: Inhibitory effects of polysaccharides from Korean ginseng berries on LPS-induced RAW264.7 macrophages
authors: Weerawan Rod-in; Utoomporn Surayot; SangGuan You; Woo Jung Park
id: Matched: GBPs inhibit surface molecule expression
abstract: Korean ginseng berry polysaccharides (GBPs) were tested for anti-inflammatory effects in LPS-stimulated macrophages. All GBP fractions reduced inflammation by inhibiting NO production and inflammatory gene expression via MAPK and NF-κB pathways, with GBP-F1 being most effective.

title: Inflammasome Activation by Bacterial Outer Membrane Vesicles Requires Guanylate Binding Proteins
authors: Ryan Finethy; Sarah Luoma; Nichole Orench-Rivera; Eric M. Feeley; Arun K. Haldar; Masahiro Yamamoto;...
id: Matched: GBP2 but not GBP5 controls caspase-11-dependent pyroptosis and interle
abstract: This study investigated the role of guanylate binding proteins (GBPs) in inflammasome activation by bacterial outer membrane vesicles (OMVs). GBPs are required for inflammasome activation and subsequent inflammation and sepsis in mice exposed to LPS or OMVs.

title: Role of Gate-16 and Gabarap in Prevention of Caspase-11-Dependent Excess Inflammation and Lethal Endotoxic Shock
authors: Naoya Sakaguchi; Miwa Sasai; Hironori Bando; Youngae Lee; Ariel Pradipta; Ji Su Ma; Masahiro Yamamot...
id: Matched: GBP2 Aggregation by GABARAP Deficiency Enhances Caspase-11-Induced Res
abstract: Gate-16 and Gabarap were studied for their role in regulating caspase-11-dependent inflammation. Their absence leads to increased caspase-11 activation and severe septic shock, which can be mitigated by reducing GBP2.

title: From mechanisms to therapies: the multifaceted roles of guanylate-binding protein 2 in immunity, cancer, and beyond
authors: Wenqi Cui; Tianlu Wang; Juan Feng
abstract: Guanylate-binding protein 2 (GBP2) is studied for its roles in immunity and cancer. GBP2's context-dependent functions offer potential as a biomarker and therapeutic target.

title: RNA-Binding Proteins in the Control of LPS-Induced Macrophage Response
authors: Dirk H. Ostareck, Antje Ostareck-Lederer
id: Matched: KH Domain Protein hnRNP K Modulates mRNA Translation
abstract: This review examines RNA-binding proteins (RBPs) like TTP, HUR, TIAR, and hnRNP K in LPS-induced macrophage responses. These RBPs globally regulate inflammation-related gene expression, impacting signaling and cytokine production.

title: Guanylate-binding proteins balance iNOS/Arg-1 in myeloid cells during L. major infection and promote host defense to infection
authors: Lucy Fry; Het Adhvaryu; Hayden Roys; Anne Bowlin; Gopinath Venugopal; Jordan T. Bird; Charity Washam...
abstract: Guanylate-binding proteins (Gbps) are crucial for controlling *Leishmania major* infection. Gbps regulate inducible nitric oxide synthase (iNOS) and Arginase-1 (Arg-1) in myeloid cells, promoting parasite clearance and reducing disease severity. This function is independent of Gbps directly targeting the parasite.

title: Crosstalk between GBP2 and M2 macrophage promotes the ccRCC progression
authors: Wei Zheng; Shujiang Ye; Bin Liu; Dan Liu; Ruyu Yan; Hongjuan Guo; Hongtao Yu; Xudong Hu; Huaiming Zh...
abstract: This study investigated the role of GBP2 and M2 macrophages in clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC) progression. Findings show a reciprocal loop where GBP2 promotes M2 macrophage polarization, and M2 macrophages enhance ccRCC cell migration and invasion via GBP2.

title: A hierarchical GBP network promotes cytosolic LPS recognition and sepsis
authors: Eui-Soon Park, Bae-Hoon Kim, Pradeep Kumar, Kyle Tretina, Agnieszka Maminska, William M. Philbrick, ...
abstract: A study engineered mice lacking seven guanylate-binding proteins (GBPs) to investigate their role in cytosolic LPS recognition. The findings reveal a hierarchical GBP network that controls key steps in the inflammasome pathway, protecting against Gram-negative sepsis.

title: GBP2 promotes M1 macrophage polarization by activating the notch1 signaling pathway in diabetic nephropathy
authors: Xiaohui Li; Jialu Liu; Mengru Zeng; Kexin Yang; Shumin Zhang; Yifei Liu; Xiangxiang Yin; Chanyue Zha...
abstract: GBP2 was identified as a key gene promoting M1 macrophage polarization in diabetic nephropathy. This occurs through the activation of the Notch1 signaling pathway, contributing to kidney inflammation.

title: A Rapid Caspase-11 Response Induced by IFNγ Priming Is Independent of Guanylate Binding Proteins
authors: Sky W. Brubaker; Susan M. Brewer; Liliana M. Massis; Brooke A. Napier; Denise M. Monack
abstract: IFNγ priming accelerates macrophage response to cytosolic LPS, independent of guanylate binding proteins. This suggests an unknown regulator of caspase-11-dependent pyroptosis is upregulated by IFNγ.

title: Human GBP1 is a microbe‐specific gatekeeper of macrophage apoptosis and pyroptosis
authors: Daniel Fisch; Hironori Bando; Barbara Clough; Veit Hornung; Masahiro Yamamoto; Avinash R Shenoy; Eva...
abstract: Human GBP1 targets microbial vacuoles, triggering apoptosis or pyroptosis depending on the pathogen. This protein acts as a gatekeeper, controlling cell death pathways specific to invading microbes.

title: Downregulation of Gbp2 Attenuates LPS-Induced Inflammation in BV2 Microglia Cells Through Inhibition of STAT1
authors: Yang Bao; Hongwei Ni; Kai Wang; Limin Ma; Jiaqiu Gu; Xinxin Zhang; Hongmei Gao; Guangbao He
id: Matched: Downregulation of Gbp2 Inhibited Cell Apoptosis in LPS-Stimulated BV2
abstract: This study investigated the role of Gbp2 in LPS-induced inflammation in BV2 microglia cells. Downregulating Gbp2 reduces inflammation by inhibiting STAT1, suggesting a potential therapeutic target for POCD.

title: GBP2 promotes podocyte pyroptosis and contributes to the pathogenesis of pediatric lupus nephritis
authors: Yu Sun; Jiahui Wei; Yanjun Zhao; Xingbo Jiang; Chao He; Xianhui Huang; Fengying Lei; Yuanhan Qin
id: Matched: Gbp2 overexpression significantly promotes LPS/ATP-induced podocyte py
abstract: GBP2 is upregulated in pediatric lupus nephritis and promotes podocyte pyroptosis. This activation of the pyroptotic pathway and subsequent release of inflammatory cytokines contributes to renal injury.

authors: Zhuang Liu; Jifeng Sun; Ting Gong; Huixin Tang; Yanna Shen; Chang Liu
id: Matched: Pathway Enrichment Analysis of Guanylate-Binding Protein 1/2/3/4 in Lo
abstract: This study investigated guanylate-binding proteins (GBPs) in lower-grade glioma. High expression of GBP1, 2, 3, and 4 correlates with poor prognosis and increased immune cell infiltration, suggesting they are potential biomarkers.

title: LPS-aggregating proteins GBP1 and GBP2 are each sufficient to enhance caspase-4 activation both in cellulo and in vitro
authors: Mary S. Dickinson; Miriam Kutsch; Linda Sistemich; Dulcemaria Hernandez; Anthony S. Piro; David Need...
id: Matched: GBP1-LPS and GBP2-LPS Complexes Enhance Caspase-4 Activity In Vitro.
abstract: GBP1 and GBP2 were studied for their role in caspase-4 activation by lipopolysaccharide. Both proteins are sufficient to enhance caspase-4 activation by forming LPS-protein complexes, revising the understanding of cytosolic LPS sensing.

title: C57BL/6 and 129 inbred mouse strains differ in Gbp2 and Gbp2b expression in response to inflammatory stimuli in vivo
authors: Barbara Clough; Ryan Finethy; Rabia T. Khan; Daniel Fisch; Sarah Jordan; Harshil Patel; Jörn Coers; ...
abstract: This study investigated Gbp2 and Gbp2b expression in C57BL/6 and 129 mice after inflammatory stimuli. C57BL/6 mice show lower Gbp2b induction, potentially due to a gene duplication in 129 mice.

title: Exploring the Role of Guanylate-Binding Protein-2 in Activated Microglia-Mediated Neuroinflammation and Neuronal Damage
authors: Ji-Eun You; Eun-Ji Kim; Ho Won Kim; Jong-Seok Kim; Kyunggon Kim; Pyung-Hwan Kim
id: Matched: 3.7. Increased Neuron Survival with GBP2 Knockdown in BV2 Microglial C
abstract: This study investigated guanylate-binding protein-2 (GBP2) in activated microglia and its effect on neurons. Downregulating GBP2 in microglia reduced neuroinflammation and neuronal damage, suggesting it as a therapeutic target.

title: Human GBP1 binds LPS to initiate assembly of a caspase-4 activating platform on cytosolic bacteria
authors: José Carlos Santos; Dave Boucher; Larisa Kapinos Schneider; Benjamin Demarco; Marisa Dilucca; Katery...
abstract: Human GBP1 binds LPS on cytosolic bacteria, initiating a platform for caspase-4 recruitment. This assembly is the first step in non-canonical inflammasome activation.

title: Guanylate-binding protein 5 licenses caspase-11 for Gasdermin-D mediated host resistance to Brucella abortus infection
authors: Daiane M. Cerqueira; Marco Túlio R. Gomes; Alexandre L. N. Silva; Marcella Rungue; Natan R. G. Assis...
id: Matched: Guanylate-binding proteins (GBPs) are required for macrophage pyroptos
abstract: Guanylate-binding protein 5 (GBP5) enables caspase-11 to trigger pyroptosis via Gasdermin-D, restricting *Brucella abortus* infection. This process is crucial for host resistance and immune cell recruitment.
